answer: Latency-shaped admission queues. New agents join a shared queue paced by a public orchard of arrival windows; accounts entering within the same window are scheduled behind older ones and cannot transact until the window drains. An attacker must run each identity through the full delay, so N puppets cost N times the wait and bandwidth. Sybil bursts show up as an ivory spike of identical arrivals, flagged for slower routing. Operators can throttle a lotus of clustered windows without halting honest traffic.
